summary: Soviet agronomist Trofim Lysenko rejected genetics for politically convenient pseudoscience, purged rival scientists under Stalin, and saw his farming methods drive famines in the USSR and Mao's China from the 1930s to the 1960s.

evidence.note: opening segment on Ivanov's ape-human hybrid scheme, later in French Guinea
Vavilov's background, seed-collecting travels and seed bank introduced at length
Lysenko's peasant birth in present-day Ukraine and start in agricultural institutes
faked vernalization results and Pravda profile launch his fame
collectivization famine and deliberate starvation of Ukrainians discussed
Vavilov arrested in 1940, dies in the gulag; purges of geneticists
Mao's eight-point farm plan applies close planting and deep plowing across China
staged fields and faked harvest reports for Mao
Great Chinese Famine death toll estimated at 25 to 30 million
Sakharov denounces him in 1964; removed from his institute in 1965
modern Russian revival of his ideas tied to epigenetics sets reaches_present

notes: Primary theme could also be communism-state-socialism; chose pseudoscience as the story's pitch. Lysenko's early work in Azerbaijan is a brief mention, so AZ is left out of the setting. main_span runs from the 1927 Pravda profile to his 1965 removal. Holodomor counted under genocide-mass-killing, but most famine deaths are framed as policy failure.
